questions.question: What is the first conditional used for?
questions.explanation: First conditional is for possible future situations: "If it rains, I will stay home."

questions.question: Complete: "If I ___ rich, I would travel the world."
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses past tense in the if-clause: "If I were rich..."

questions.question: Which is a zero conditional?
options: If you heat water, it boils.
If it rains, I will stay home.
If I were you, I would study.
If I had known, I would have helped.
questions.explanation: Zero conditional is for facts: "If you heat water, it boils" (always true).

questions.question: Which word can replace "if" in the sentence "If you dont hurry, you will be late"?
questions.explanation: "Unless" means "if not": "Unless you hurry, you will be late."

questions.question: What is wrong with: "If it will rain, I stay home"?
questions.explanation: In first conditional, dont use "will" in the if-clause. Use present tense.
